implementation.name: Squirrel standalone interpreter/embeddable VM
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Application and game scripting embedded in a host VM.

prerequisites.text: Learn dynamic values, closures and the host's exposed API.

execution.text: The standalone sq interpreter executes scripts; a C API embeds the VM.

behavior.text: Classes and callable values support dynamic application extensions.

tooling.text: The distribution supplies a standalone interpreter and an embedding API.

maintenance.text: A host controls exposed functions; standalone scripts do not automatically have game-specific APIs.

costs.text: The VM's MIT license is separate from the host application's libraries and content.

example.run_instructions: With the standalone Squirrel interpreter installed, run sq hello.nut.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: Retain copyright and permission notices for the VM component.

implementation.name: Standard ML of New Jersey (SML/NJ)
implementation.version_scope: Standard ML '97 in SML/NJ; interactive guide and release information checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: SML/NJ compiles Standard ML '97 and supplies libraries and development tools; this profile describes that implementation.

prerequisites.text: Learn declarations, types and expressions, then use the interactive system to inspect their inferred types.

execution.text: The sml command starts a REPL; use loads a source file, while Compilation Manager organizes larger programs.

behavior.text: Type mismatches are compiler errors; interactive expressions are bound to it and declarations expose their types.

tooling.text: Compilation Manager and source-position diagnostics support work beyond isolated REPL expressions.

maintenance.text: SML/NJ publishes separate development and legacy release information; select the matching distribution and documentation.

costs.text: The SML/NJ license permits use and distribution without a fee, with notice and publicity conditions.

example.run_instructions: Save addition.sml, start sml in that directory, and enter use "addition.sml"; at the prompt.
example.expected_result: Prints 5, alongside the interactive compiler's binding and loading messages.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: Applies to SML/NJ's covered implementation files; retain the required copyright, permission and disclaimer notices.

implementation.name: Starlark in Go
implementation.version_scope: Go interpreter documentation checked on 2026-10-13; embedding hosts can expose different APIs.

sources.label: Starlark in Go documentation and CLI

fit.text: An embeddable configuration language for structured data and application scripting; Bazel is one host rather than the whole language.

prerequisites.text: Learn Python-like expressions, functions and collections, then the particular host's additional built-ins.

execution.text: The Go implementation provides a standalone interpreter and a Go API for executing files.

behavior.text: Starlark uses dynamic values and lexical functions; host applications decide which domain-specific operations are available.

tooling.text: The starlark CLI offers a REPL; Go applications can call ExecFile and retrieve module globals.

maintenance.text: Record the Go interpreter revision and host API together, since host extensions affect portability.

costs.text: The selected Go interpreter uses BSD-3-Clause; the Bazel host and application dependencies have separate licenses.

example.run_instructions: With the documented starlark CLI installed, run starlark total.star.
example.expected_result: Prints 5; no Bazel-specific built-ins are required.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: Retain the license notices and disclaimer; the grant covers the Go interpreter, not every Starlark host.

implementation.name: SuperCollider sclang
implementation.version_scope: SuperCollider 3.14.0 tutorial and development README checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: sclang controls audio synthesis and algorithmic composition; the audio server is a separate program.

prerequisites.text: Learn objects, messages and code evaluation before adding audio-server and scheduling concepts.

execution.text: The IDE sends selected code to sclang; synthesis uses scsynth or supernova communicating through OSC.

behavior.text: Evaluation posts the last expression's result; postln explicitly writes a value to the post window.

tooling.text: The IDE includes help, Quarks manages language extensions, and servers can load separate native plugins.

maintenance.text: Match tutorials, language extensions and server plugins to the installed distribution rather than mixing development snapshots.

costs.text: The distribution declares GNU GPL version 3; bundled libraries and plugins require their own notices.

example.run_instructions: Save hello.scd in the SuperCollider IDE and evaluate the line using the platform's documented evaluation shortcut.
example.expected_result: PLLDN appears in the post window; the IDE may also display the expression's returned string. This example does not start audio synthesis.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: The checked COPYING contains GNU GPL version 3, but a complete per-file version-choice and dependency license inventory is not established here.

implementation.name: Swift compiler and Swift Package Manager
implementation.version_scope: Swift.org CLI tutorial and language-book sources checked on 2026-10-13.

sources.label: Swift implementation license and runtime exception

fit.text: The project documents command-line tools, libraries, web services and Apple applications; those workflows have different host requirements.

prerequisites.text: Install the platform toolchain and learn constants, variables and type inference; Apple application tutorials additionally require macOS and Xcode.

execution.text: SwiftPM creates an executable package and compiles and runs it with swift run.

behavior.text: Swift checks types and can infer them from initial values; top-level code in main.swift can be an entry point.

tooling.text: SwiftPM manages package manifests and dependencies; Package.resolved records resolved package versions.

maintenance.text: Keep the selected toolchain and package versions with the project; application framework availability depends on the target.

costs.text: The compiler source has Apache-2.0 with the Swift runtime-library exception; SDKs and packages retain separate terms.

example.run_instructions: Create an executable package with swift package init --name PLLDNExample --type executable. Put this code in its generated Sources/main.swift and run swift run PLLDNExample.

implementation.name: TLA+ specification language with TLC and Toolbox
implementation.version_scope: TLA+ high-level overview and TLC/Toolbox documentation checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: TLA+ describes possible system behaviors mathematically and checks models of concurrent algorithms; it is not an application implementation.

prerequisites.text: Learn state predicates, next-state relations and temporal formulas; the documented tools require Java 11 or later.

execution.text: TLC explores a configured model; the Toolbox accepts either Init and Next or a single temporal behavior formula.

behavior.text: Invariants are state predicates checked over reachable states; a finite model check is scoped to that model.

tooling.text: The repository supplies CLI tools and the Toolbox; the proof manager is a separate project.

maintenance.text: Preserve the specification, model constants and checking options together so the checked state space is identifiable.

costs.text: The selected TLA+ tools are MIT-licensed; Java and any separately installed proof tools have their own licenses.

example.code:
---- MODULE Toggle ----
VARIABLE on
Init == on = FALSE
Next == on' = ~on
TypeOK == on \in BOOLEAN
====
example.run_instructions: Open Toggle.tla as a Toolbox specification, create a model using Init and Next, add TypeOK as an invariant, and run TLC.
example.expected_result: The model alternates between FALSE and TRUE; TLC should explore two distinct states and find TypeOK true for this finite model.

licenses.component: TLA+ specification language with TLC and Toolbox
licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: This identifies the tlaplus/tlaplus implementation repository's grant; it does not assign a license to all specifications written in TLA+.

implementation.name: Tcl core interpreter (tclsh)
implementation.version_scope: Tcl 9.0 command and shell manuals checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: tclsh evaluates Tcl command scripts and supports interactive use; graphical Tk applications use an additional toolkit.

prerequisites.text: Install a Tcl interpreter matching the manual and learn command arguments, substitutions and channels.

execution.text: tclsh reads a script filename or starts interactively when no filename is supplied.

behavior.text: Script arguments appear in argv; puts writes to a channel and defaults to standard output.

tooling.text: The shell exposes a REPL and can source other Tcl files; versioned executable names permit multiple installations.

maintenance.text: Record the interpreter version and installed packages; a script should not assume every Tcl installation has the same extensions.

costs.text: The Tcl core grant requires retained notices and no royalty fee for authorized uses; exceptions in individual files remain relevant.

example.run_instructions: With Tcl 9.0 installed, run tclsh hello.tcl, using the installed versioned executable name if necessary.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: The core license explicitly permits per-file exceptions and differently licensed modifications; Tk and external extensions are outside this entry.

implementation.name: Terra language implementation
implementation.version_scope: Terra getting-started documentation and release license checked on 2026-10-13.

sources.label: Terra getting started and Lua interaction

fit.text: Terra embeds a statically typed low-level language in Lua for generated native code and C-library integration.

prerequisites.text: Learn Lua's top-level execution and Terra's typed function declarations; install a Terra distribution with its compiler dependencies.

execution.text: Lua runs top-level statements, while called Terra functions are JIT-compiled to machine code.

behavior.text: Terra arguments have declared types and return types may be inferred; a top-level print by itself is Lua code.

tooling.text: The terra executable runs .t files or a Lua-like REPL; bundled examples demonstrate language features.

maintenance.text: Keep the Terra distribution and LLVM/C integration requirements together when reproducing generated code.

costs.text: The Terra release grant is MIT; LLVM, Lua and linked native libraries require separate license review.

example.code:
terra total(a : int, b : int)
    return a + b
end
print(total(2, 3))
example.run_instructions: Using the Terra distribution's executable, run terra total.t, or its documented bin/terra path.
example.expected_result: Calls the Terra function from Lua and prints 5.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: The release license covers Terra's software; retain its copyright and permission notice and review dependency notices separately.

implementation.name: TypeScript compiler with Node.js
implementation.version_scope: Compiler-to-JavaScript workflow; runtime and compiler versions are separate choices.

sources.label: TypeScript: JavaScript prerequisites and erased types
TypeScript compiler CLI and explicit configuration handling

fit.text: Typed browser and server application code in the JavaScript ecosystem; the host still determines available APIs.

prerequisites.text: Learn JavaScript syntax and runtime behavior alongside static types. Existing JavaScript experience changes the learning path.

execution.text: The compiler checks .ts files and emits JavaScript; Node.js or a browser executes that output.

behavior.text: Type annotations are erased. A declared type alone does not validate incoming data at runtime.

tooling.text: Use tsc and tsconfig settings for compiler checks; strictness controls how much checking is performed.

maintenance.text: Keep the JavaScript target and host APIs aligned; compiler type checks can be stricter than valid JavaScript execution.

costs.text: Plan for compiler configuration and the chosen JavaScript deployment host. The compiler license and hosting arrangement are separate.

example.run_instructions: With TypeScript and Node.js installed, run tsc --strict --target ES2022 hello.ts from a directory without tsconfig.json, then node hello.js. For a standalone file inside a configured project with TypeScript 6 or later, add --ignoreConfig; use tsc -p for the project's own configuration.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: The compiler source covered by its LICENSE.txt.
licenses.notice: Read Apache-2.0 terms; this is not the license of applications compiled with it.

licenses.scope: Node.js core grant only; bundled components have additional notices in this file.
licenses.notice: Review the full runtime distribution and each application dependency separately.

implementation.name: V compiler
implementation.version_scope: V documentation on the checked master branch, 2026-10-13; pre-1.0 language-reference rules are documented.

fit.text: V is a statically typed compiled language for application code; its documentation and compiler tests define the current language reference.

prerequisites.text: Install the V compiler and its platform build prerequisites, then learn functions, types and module organization.

execution.text: v run compiles and executes a file; v followed by a filename compiles without executing it.

behavior.text: Files in the same module directory can share declarations without importing sibling files.

tooling.text: The compiler provides run, build and help commands; a .vvmrc can select a project-local compiler version.

maintenance.text: The documentation states that compiler behavior and tests govern discrepancies before 1.0; pin the compiler for reproducible work.

costs.text: The compiler repository uses MIT; imported modules and native dependencies can have separate license obligations.

example.run_instructions: With the selected V compiler on PATH, run v run hello.v.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: MIT applies to the selected compiler repository's covered files; preserve its notices and inspect imported packages separately.
